kurz: Building a set of rules that a stranger could read and execute, and the calculation of when the effort pays off.

bloecke.md:
A set-up is more than a picture of the market. It is a decision protocol that is complete before any money is at stake. A simple and strict test shows whether it meets this standard. A third party would have to be able to read the set of rules and place the same orders without asking any questions. Phrases such as “if the breakout looks clean”, “when market conditions are good” or “as long as the environment is right” fail this test. They define nothing and postpone the decision to a later point, when it is made under pressure.

The second reason for putting it in writing has to do with memory. Hindsight bias (Fischhoff 1975) systematically shifts the memory of your own expectation towards what actually happened later. Three months on, nobody knows any more whether an entry followed from the rule or from a feeling, unless the reason was noted down with a date. The journal is therefore the only reliable protection against this distortion of your own memory.

bloecke.titel: Set of rules, execution per trade and review
bloecke.unter: The left-hand column is written once, the middle one is applied to every trade and the right-hand one is reviewed quarterly. Changes are made at only one point and only as scheduled.

bloecke.md:
## Universe and signal

The universe defines which securities are eligible for trading. It is based on verifiable criteria such as index membership, average daily turnover on Xetra and minimum price, and it excludes securities with an upcoming corporate action. Two German peculiarities are part of this. First, the volume of a security is spread across Xetra, regional exchanges, off-exchange trading and foreign stock exchanges. A volume bar from a single broker's chart therefore does not reflect the whole market. Second, continuous trading on Xetra runs from 9:00 to 17:30. Before and after, spreads are wider and turnover is lower, and breakouts in these fringe hours are more often a consequence of low liquidity than a signal. A complete universe therefore includes a trading time window.

The signal rule must be worded so that it can be applied to historical data without anyone judging by eye. It also includes an exclusion condition, which is almost always missing. This condition defines when a signal that has been triggered nevertheless does not apply, for example on the day before quarterly results, in the case of a price gap above a set percentage or when three positions from the same sector are already open.

Entry, stop and target are set at the same time, before the order is placed. If a stop is only determined afterwards, it is based on the price and not on the set of rules. The set of rules also includes a time stop. A position that has reached neither the target nor the stop after n days is closed. Without a time stop, any failed trade can turn unnoticed into a long-term investment.

## Minimum capital and fixed costs

There is no legal minimum for a trading account. The practical minimum results from the ratio of fixed costs to risk per trade. The number of units is calculated from the risk in euros and the stop distance and is not chosen by gut feeling. The smaller the account, the smaller the position, while the order fee stays the same.

The following illustrative calculation assumes 1% risk per trade, a stop 8% below the entry, an order fee of €2 for purchase and sale combined and 0.10% of the position value for spread and slippage across both sides. The position size is therefore always 0.125 times the capital.

bloecke.titel: Costs per round turn relative to risk per trade (illustrative calculation)
kopf: As a share of the risk

bloecke.md: The most important message of the table is in the last column. For an assumed strategy with a 40% hit rate and a reward-to-risk ratio of 2, the expected value before costs is 0.2 R per trade, that is, 20% of the risk taken. With €2,000 of capital, trading costs consume 11.25 of these 20 percentage points, that is, more than half of the assumed edge. With €50,000, it is 8.25% of the expected value. A floor remains in every case. Regardless of account size, the variable costs of 0.10% amount to 1.25% of the risk, that is, 6.25% of the expected value.

bloecke.titel: Trading costs as a share of the assumed expected value
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation based on the table, with an expected value of 0.2 R per trade. The influence of account size is due to the fixed costs; below around €10,000, the order fee dominates.

bloecke.md:
## Journal and review

A journal that only records entry, exit and result is merely a statement of account. A review requires three further fields. Before execution, the reason for the signal is entered in one sentence together with the expected range of the result; after the exit, a flag is added showing whether or not the trade complied with the rules. Only this third field shows whether losses stem from the strategy or from a lack of discipline. These are two different problems with different consequences.

The expected range is included because overprecision is one of the most robust findings of decision research. People systematically choose estimation intervals that are too narrow. Comparing a recorded range with what actually happened twelve months later is the cheapest calibration exercise available.

With a 50% loss rate per trade, there is an 81% probability of at least one streak of five consecutive losses in 100 independent trades, and with a 60% loss rate the probability is 97.6%. A streak of six losses still has a probability of 54.6% at 50%. Switching strategy after such a streak is a reaction to noise, and the sample starts again from scratch. Conversely, a winning streak is no proof of skill.

## Required sample size

With a 40% hit rate and a reward-to-risk ratio of 2, a trade ends either at +2 R or at −1 R. The expected value is 0.2 R, the standard deviation 1.47 R. The noise is therefore more than seven times as large as the signal. From this it follows directly how many trades are needed to distinguish the expected value from zero.

bloecke.erklaerung: Number of trades needed for the measured average gain to reach the required t-value. Because the expression in brackets is squared, halving the edge quadruples the required sample size.
variablen: expected value per trade in R-multiples
standard deviation of the individual results in R-multiples
required t-value; 2.0 for a single test specified in advance
bloecke.beispiel: E = 0.2 R, s = 1.47 R, t = 2: n = (2 × 1.47 / 0.2)² = 216 trades. For t = 3.0, it is 486 trades. Harvey, Liu and Zhu (2016) call for this hurdle because of the large number of strategies tested.

bloecke.titel: Required number of trades depending on the size of the edge
bloecke.unter: Calculated using n = (t × s / E)² with s = 1.47 R; the y-axis is logarithmic. With an edge of 0.1 R instead of 0.2 R, the requirement rises from 216 to 864 trades.

bloecke.titel: Hourly rate in the best case
bloecke.md:
The example assumes €25,000 of capital, 100 trades a year and an expected value of 0.2 R with R = €250.

The gross result is 100 × 0.2 × €250 = €5,000. After trading costs of 100 × €5.13 = €513, €4,487 remains before tax. After deducting the saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag), €3,487 of this is taxable. The flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) of 26.375% amounts to €920, leaving around €3,567 net.

For the time spent, 30 minutes of preparation on around 250 trading days is assumed (125 hours), plus 10 minutes of record-keeping per trade (17 hours) and four quarterly reviews of 3 hours each (12 hours). That is around 154 hours in total, or around €23 per hour.

This calculation assumes that the edge exists. Since 216 trades are needed to prove it, it takes just over two years to establish whether it existed.

Under the flat-rate withholding tax, Section 20(9) EStG (Income Tax Act) excludes the deduction of income-related expenses (Werbungskosten). Only the saver's allowance of €1,000, or €2,000 for joint assessment, is deductible. Data feeds, charting software, courses and literature therefore do not reduce the tax. Above the allowance, every euro of fixed costs has to be earned with €1.36 of profit before tax, because 1 ÷ (1 − 0.26375) = 1.36. The 26.375% is made up of 25% capital income withholding tax (Kapitalertragsteuer) under Section 43a(1) EStG and a 5.5% solidarity surcharge on it under Section 4 SolzG 1995 (Solidarity Surcharge Act). With church tax, it is 27.82% or 27.995%. Investors who trade with several banks must also make sure themselves that losses are taken into account. The loss certificate (Verlustbescheinigung) under Section 43a(3) sentences 4 and 5 EStG must be applied for by 15 December, and the application is irrevocable.

## Setting stopping criteria in advance

A stopping criterion that is only formulated during a drawdown does not serve its purpose. It must be fixed beforehand, with a figure and a deadline, and be tied to measures that are not determined by the chance outcome of individual trades. The asymmetry of recovery gives an indication of the order of magnitude. After a 20% loss, a 25% gain is needed to make it up, after a 30% loss already 42.9% and after a 50% loss 100%.

bloecke.titel: Four stopping criteria that can be set in advance
zeilen: Drawdown of the trading account from its peak
suspend trading at the set threshold, resume only after a written review
Share of trades in the journal that broke the rules
above the threshold, the problem does not lie in the strategy, so pause instead of changing the rules
Expected value per trade after the minimum number of trades set in advance
if the interval still includes zero, nothing has been proven
Hours per year against net result after tax
below the self-imposed hourly rate, the strategy is abandoned, regardless of the sign of the result

bloecke.md:
## Abstaining as the default

In Taiwan, day traders as a group were in the red after fees in every single one of the 15 years studied. More than 75% gave up within two years, and less than 1% showed predictably profitable performance. In Brazil, 97% of those who persisted for more than 300 trading days lost money, and 1.1% earned more than the minimum wage. These figures describe day traders as a whole and not just beginners.

A ban on trading cannot be derived from this. The findings do, however, determine who bears the burden of proof. Active traders bear it compared with the simple alternative of leaving the same money untouched. This burden of proof can be quantified: 216 trades with an edge of 0.2 R and 864 with an edge of 0.1 R, each with a journal that also tracks rule compliance. An investor who is not willing to put in this effort in terms of time, money and attention has thereby already made a decision. Abstaining is a fully valid decision and the only result that is certain without a sample.

mitnehmen: A set of rules only serves its purpose if a stranger could read it and place the same orders without asking questions.
The minimum capital follows from the fixed costs, because in the illustrative calculation trading costs consume 56% of an assumed edge of 0.2 R with an account of €2,000, and still 8% with €50,000.
Because the noise is greater than the signal, proof requires around 216 trades with an expected value of 0.2 R, and around 864 with half the edge.

A losing streak is not a suitable stopping criterion, because with a 50% loss rate, five consecutive losses occur in 100 trades with a probability of 81%. Suitable stopping criteria are tied to drawdown, rule compliance, statistics and effort.
Fixed costs are not deductible under the flat-rate withholding tax (Section 20(9) EStG), so every euro of them has to be earned with €1.36 of profit before tax.

begriffe.text: Set of tradable securities defined in advance, including a trading time window. It is defined using verifiable criteria such as index membership, minimum turnover and minimum price and not by an estimate made by eye.

Record that captures the signal reason and the expected range of outcomes before execution and notes after the exit whether the trade complied with the rules. It is the only reliable countermeasure against hindsight bias and overprecision.

Trade that was executed even though the written set of rules did not provide for it, or provided for it differently. The share of such trades in the journal shows whether there is a strategy problem or a discipline problem.
Threshold for drawdown, rule compliance, statistical proof or time spent, set in advance and in writing. When it is reached, trading is suspended without any fresh debate at that moment.

Number of trades needed for a measured average gain to be distinguishable from zero, calculated as n = (t × s / E)². Because E appears squared in the denominator, halving the edge quadruples the requirement.
